title: Unemployment Benefit Claims Training Note: Aligning a Payment Election to the Payment Cycle
content:
**What decides the alignment?** On an Unemployment Benefit Claims record, the election lead time of a payment election is aligned according to how the latest payment on the claim was issued. The latest payment is the payment with the latest issue date on the claim.

**What is the alignment for each method?**

| Latest payment on the claim | Election lead time |
|---|---|
| Issued by paper check | Rounded up to a whole multiple of the paper-check cycle of 5 business days |
| Issued to the state benefit debit card | Increased by 2 card activation days, with no rounding |
| Issued by direct deposit, or no payment issued | Stands as counted |

**When is the alignment applied?** Last: it acts on the whole election lead time as counted, and nothing is added after it.

**Hypothetical cases.**

| Lead time as counted | Latest payment | Aligned lead time |
|---|---|---|
| 3 business days | Paper check | 5 |
| 5 business days | Paper check | 5 |
| 6 business days | Paper check | 10 |
| 3 business days | State benefit debit card | 5 |
| 3 business days | Direct deposit to checking | 3 |
| 3 business days | None issued | 3 |
